author: Evagrius Ponticus
addressee: one who has been deemed worthy of knowledge
occasion: A collection of practical and doctrinal counsels for an advanced Christian ascetic who has been granted spiritual knowledge, guiding him in conduct, teaching, and contemplation.
argument: Evagrius distinguishes the practical ascetic, who has calmed the passionate part of the soul, from the gnostic, who has received knowledge by God's grace and must guard it through virtue, especially freedom from anger. The gnostic must avoid lawsuits, love of money, harshness, and careless speech about divine things, while discerning when and to whom to speak. He must train his mind against false thoughts and learn from approved teachers such as Gregory, Basil, Athanasius, Sarapion, and Didymus. The work closes with the counsel to keep looking to the archetype and to write its images without omitting anything that helps recover what has fallen.

outline.move: Defines the gnostic in contrast to the practical ascetic, describes the two kinds of knowledge, and gives initial counsels on virtue, condescension, lawsuits, and speaking appropriately to monks and worldly people about right conduct and natural and theological doctrines in part.
Warns against allegorizing the words of blameworthy persons, urges the gnostic to be approachable, and gives counsels on guarding secrets, avoiding careless theology, money, anger, and slander.

Counsels discretion about judgment, bodily discipline, freedom from anxiety about food and clothing, silence before the ineffable Trinity, and identifies the gnostic's temptation as false supposition in the mind.
Reports teachings on the four virtues and on knowledge from Gregory, Basil, Athanasius, Sarapion, and Didymus, and closes with the counsel to keep looking to the archetype.

cast.name: Evagrius Ponticus
cast.who: The author, a monastic teacher presenting counsels to an advanced ascetic.

cast.name: Gregory
cast.who: Gregory the Theologian, cited as the source of the teaching on the four virtues.

cast.name: Basil
cast.who: Basil of Caesarea, cited on the two kinds of knowledge.

cast.name: Athanasius
cast.who: Athanasius of Alexandria, cited on the table of Moses and enduring temptation.

cast.name: Sarapion
cast.who: Bishop of Thmuis, cited on the mind, love, and self-control.

cast.name: Didymus
cast.who: Didymus the Blind, cited on training the mind in discourses on providence and judgment.

cast.name: Balaam
cast.who: A blameworthy figure who spoke prophetically about the Savior's origin by God's dispensation.

cast.name: Caiaphas
cast.who: One of the blameworthy persons whose words were used by God's dispensation; he spoke prophetically about the Savior's death.

cast.name: Abenner
cast.who: A Levite who received the ark of the Lord and became rich and honored.

voices.speaker: Gregory
voices.how_marked: Introduced as 'the just Gregory' and reported with 'we have learned' (μεμαθήκαμεν) and 'he used to say' (ἔλεγεν).

voices.speaker: Basil
voices.how_marked: Introduced as 'Basil the Cappadocian, pillar of truth' and quoted with 'he says'.

voices.speaker: Athanasius
voices.how_marked: Introduced as 'the holy luminary of the Egyptians Athanasius' and quoted with 'he says'.

voices.speaker: Sarapion
voices.how_marked: Introduced as 'the angel of the church of the Thmuites Sarapion' and reported with 'he used to say' (Ἔλεγεν).

voices.speaker: Didymus
voices.how_marked: Introduced as 'the great and gnostic teacher Didymus' and quoted with 'he says'.

key_terms.sense: The advanced Christian who has received spiritual knowledge by God's grace and lives accordingly.
The ascetic who has calmed the passionate part of the soul but has not yet attained spiritual knowledge.
Spiritual knowledge given by God's grace, distinct from ordinary external learning.
Freedom from the passions, the state of the practical ascetic and the prerequisite for receiving divine knowledge.
Freedom from anger, the virtue most necessary for the gnostic.
Contemplation, especially of intelligible and holy realities.
The mind or intellect, the faculty that receives spiritual knowledge and is purified by it.
The principles or inner meanings of created things, known through wisdom and contemplation.
The original pattern or model to which the gnostic must look in forming images.
Condescension or accommodation to others, which the gnostic must practice without it becoming a fixed habit.
God's dispensation or special arrangement by which even blameworthy persons may speak prophetically.
Secret or ineffable teachings that must not be divulged for gain, pleasure, or passing glory.

names.Abenner: Abinadab (Septuagint variant form; standard LXX is usually Abinadab)

scripture: The author uses Septuagint book names and numbering. The ark narrative with Abenner is at 1 Samuel 7:1 in both Hebrew and Septuagint traditions. Cite as 1 Samuel, with a note that the author follows the Septuagint and uses the variant form Abenner.
uncertain: The exact date of composition within Evagrius's career.
The identity of the addressee beyond the description 'one deemed worthy of knowledge'.
The precise extent of the original work, since the surviving text is fragmentary.
Whether the section numbering gaps reflect lost material or later editorial arrangement.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Αἰσχρὸν γνωστικῷ τὸ δικάζεσθαι καὶ ἀδικουμένῳ καὶ ἀδικοῦντι
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source says it is shameful (αἰσχρόν) for the gnostic to go to law (δικάζεσθαι), whether wronged or wronging—not that he must avoid lawsuits as a practical counsel, but that it is shameful for him to engage in litigation at all.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Φιλάργυρός ἐστιν οὐχ ὁ ἔχων χρήματα, ἀλλ' ὁ ἐφιέμενος τούτων
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source distinguishes the lover of money from one who merely possesses money, defining the philargyros as one who desires money, not one who has it; it also presents the steward as a 'rational purse' (βαλάντιον λογικόν), suggesting a nuanced view rather than simple avoidance.

_unresolved_facts.claim: He must train his mind against false thoughts
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Πειρασμὸς γνωστικοῦ ἐστιν ὑπόληψις ψευδὴς περὶ τὸν νοῦν ἱσταμένη
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source defines temptation of the gnostic as false supposition (ὑπόληψις ψευδής) standing in the mind, not as something he must actively train against; it is a definition of what temptation is, not an exhortation to training.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Balaam... spoke prophetically about the Savior's origin
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὡς ἐν τῷ Βαλαὰμ καὶ Καϊάφᾳ, ἵνα ὁ μὲν περὶ γενέσεως, ὁ δὲ περὶ θανάτου τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν προείπῃ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Balaam spoke about the Savior's birth (γένεσις), not 'origin' in a general sense; Caiaphas spoke about his death. The source specifies γένεσις (birth/genesis), which is more specific than 'origin'.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Abenner... received the ark of the Lord
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: τοῦ Ἀβενὴρ τοῦ λευίτου ὃς τὴν κιβωτὸν ὑποδεξάμενος τοῦ Κυρίου
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source says Abenner 'received' (ὑποδεξάμενος) the ark, which could mean 'received' in the sense of 'took in' or 'gave lodging to'; the standard biblical narrative has the ark staying at the house of Abinadab, with his son Eleazar consecrated to guard it. The brief's claim is not wrong per se, but 'received' is more accurate than the implication of active reception.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Gregory... reported with 'we have learned' (μεμαθήκαμεν) and 'he used to say' (ἔλεγεν)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: παρὰ τοῦ δικαίου Γρηγορίου μεμαθήκαμεν... φρονήσεως μὲν ἔργον ἔλεγεν εἶναι
_unresolved_facts.fix: The 'he used to say' (ἔλεγεν) applies specifically to Gregory's teaching about the work of prudence (φρονήσεως μὲν ἔργον ἔλεγεν εἶναι), not to the whole teaching on four virtues; the four virtues are introduced with 'we have learned' (μεμαθήκαμεν), while the detailed exposition uses ἔλεγεν for specific points.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Sarapion... reported with 'he used to say' (Ἔλεγεν)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἔλεγεν ὁ τῆς Θμουϊτῶν ἐκκλησίας ἄγγελος Σαραπίων
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source uses Ἔλεγεν (imperfect, 'he was saying/used to say') for Sarapion, but the brief's claim is technically accurate; however, the more precise rendering would note this is the same verb form used for Gregory's specific points, not a general 'reported' frame.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Abenner: Abinadab (Septuagint variant form; standard LXX is usually Abinadab)
_unresolved_facts.fix: The name Ἀβενὴρ (Abenner) is not the standard LXX form for Abinadab (usually Ἀβιναδάβ). It appears to be a variant or corruption. The brief should state that this is a distinct variant form, not equate it simply with 'Abinadab' as if it were a normal LXX variant.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The ark narrative with Abenner is at 1 Samuel 7:1 in both Hebrew and Septuagint traditions
_unresolved_facts.fix: The ark narrative with Abinadab is at 1 Samuel 7:1 (Hebrew) / 1 Kingdoms 7:1 (LXX). However, the LXX text there has Ἀβιναδάβ, not Ἀβενὴρ. The author Evagrius uses a variant form Ἀβενὴρ, which does not appear at 1 Samuel 7:1 in standard LXX manuscripts. The brief should not claim this is 'in both Hebrew and Septuagint traditions' as if the name form matches.
